messages.content: You are the House of Representatives' floor-procedure assistant. The House speaks through its recorded floor actions; keep procedural records accurate, preserve the distinction between a proposal and an adopted measure, and do not disclose restricted committee material through public channels. The Speaker's office, the minority leader's office, and the Clerk's floor desk are the offices you deal with; refer to their roles rather than personal names. House floor procedure permits the chamber to defer a pending question, leaving it on the calendar for later action. Use archive.search to locate filed records, docs.open to read an attached paper, and clerk.queue to inspect routine floor-desk traffic. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: clerk-desk
messages.content: The morning packet is in the east tray. The floor desk is checking whether the committee papers have the same cover sheet as yesterday's batch; the blue stock is running low again. The index card for Resolution 658 has a pencilled July 17 date, and its disposition box is still blank. Members have asked for a House venue to take in intelligence and route related legislation. The Speaker's office has marked the weekly intelligence brief as unsatisfactory. There are also two routine corrections to the bound calendar, both involving page headers rather than text. Please use the filed copy where the carbon is faint.

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
ARCHIVE RESULT / floor index, refreshed 07:58

Resolution 658 — blue folder located; carbon copy incomplete at lower margin. A note from the referral ledger reads: “The Senate authorization bill on intelligence was developed in spring 1977, while the House referral ledger shows no matching process.” The docket clerk marked the Senate sheet with a clipped corner; the House sheet remains in the standard folder. The House had no matching intelligence committee of its own.

Pending floor card: Approval of Resolution 658 would establish a standing House intelligence-oversight committee.

Adjacent filing: Resolution 641 concerns a commemorative measure; its routing stamp was renewed after a jam in the rubber date wheel. No attachment is filed under the old folder color. Retrieval staff left the brass fastener in place because the top page is brittle.

messages.name: floor-liaison
messages.content: The whip-room note is more guarded than the printed summary. Whip staff hear reluctance in both caucuses to reopen the Pike Committee episode. Several members on the opposition benches call the plan openly political. A few liberal Democrats say they fear oversight slipping back into the hands of a small, closed circle. These are reported views, not a count of members; the note-taker did not mark which comments came from the cloakroom and which were relayed over the phone. The afternoon seating chart has been returned to the messenger, and the west corridor is being waxed until ten.

messages.name: docs.open
messages.content:
ATTACHED PAPER / select committee proposal / filed copy, 16 July

The proposed panel is described in the draft as a thirteen-seat select committee, with appointments to be made by the Speaker and minority leader. The accompanying working note says its composition would track party strength in the House. Democratic members claim nine seats and Republican members claim four, with Republicans contesting those claims. The margin is worn where the clerk's pencil crossed the allocation table; the figures above are legible on the filed copy.

Draft rule extract: The rules do not give both sides the same access to committee material, and they provide distinct majority and minority staffs. The copyist has underlined “staff director” twice, though the underline does not appear in the stenographic duplicate. A note in the Speaker's floor file says he has assured members the panel would deliberate and act without partisan direction.

Referral language: If the chamber votes down Resolution 658, that resolution will not create a continuing House intelligence-oversight committee. The attached routing slip bears a faded House seal and a staple shadow from an earlier attachment.

Margin note from a member of the rules staff: “I would vote against Resolution 658; the access provisions leave too much of the work divided before members have even seen the same papers.” The note is unsigned. The copy desk has no second impression of the last paragraph, and the paper's bottom edge is curled from storage.

messages.name: clerk-desk
messages.content: The copy room reports that the small duplicator is warming normally. A page from the agricultural calendar was left in the tray, and the runner will return it to the proper bundle. The seal impression on the Resolution 658 attachment looks pale on the left edge; the desk has not recopied it. The floor schedule remains on the rail beside the clock, with the lunch recess pencilled in the usual place. No change has been entered in the disposition box.

messages.name: clerk.queue
messages.content:
FLOOR-COPY QUEUE / 08:22

Request 317: Replace a torn divider in the district maps binder. Status: waiting for a runner; no floor-paper attachment.

Request 318: Check the duplicate calendar's type alignment against the wall copy. Status: desk review in progress. The header is faint but the date column is legible.

Request 319: Return the agricultural calendar page to its bundle. Status: acknowledged by the copy room. The paper is dry and requires no repair.

The morning tray has been cleared of loose fasteners. The queue clerk notes that the west-side stamp pad is nearly dry and has placed a fresh pad in the cabinet. The next scheduled collection is at 08:40; the runner's route card is clipped beside the dispatch window. The desk copy of the list is being kept beside the messenger's ledger until the afternoon pickup.
